issues.legal_issue: Property owned by a municipal corporation but occupied by persons other than the corporation is not exempt from property tax merely because title remains with the corporation.
material_facts: The corporation constructed houses and allotted them to occupants under hire-purchase agreements.
The agreements provided that title would remain with the corporation until the instalments were paid and conveyances executed.
The occupants had possession of and lived in the houses while the corporation retained title.
The agreements required the occupants to bear municipal taxes.
The corporation demanded house tax from the occupants before they had completed payment for the houses.
issues.conclusion: The statutory exemption for property vesting in the corporation applies only when the corporation has both title to and occupation of the property. Since the occupants, rather than the corporation, occupied the houses, the exemption did not apply, and the corporation could levy property tax, primarily from the actual occupiers.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 197(1)(i) and 199(1) of the Hyderabad Municipal Corporation Act impose the framework for levying taxes on lands and buildings. Section 202(1)(c), read in the context of that framework, exempts corporation property only when it vests in the corporation in both title and possession; the word “vest” is context-dependent, as explained in Fruit & Vegetable Merchants Union v. Delhi Improvement Trust, AIR 1954 SC 344, and Richardson v. Robertson, [1862] 6 L.T. 75. Section 204(1) provides that property taxes are primarily leviable from an actual occupier who holds the premises immediately from the corporation or government, confirming that corporation-owned premises occupied by others may be taxed.

rule.if: municipal_property_tax_levy_challenge and corporation_retained_title and noncorporate_occupants_possessed_property and occupants_held_from_corporation

predicates.municipal_property_tax_levy_challenge: A proceeding challenges a municipal corporation’s levy of property tax on premises.
predicates.corporation_retained_title: The municipal corporation retained title to the premises at the time of the tax levy.
predicates.noncorporate_occupants_possessed_propert: Persons other than the municipal corporation actually possessed and occupied the premises.
predicates.occupants_held_from_corporation: The occupants held the premises immediately from the municipal corporation.

issues.definition: When a property-tax levy is challenged, the corporation retains title, and other persons occupy the premises holding them from the corporation, the property is not exempt from property tax on the basis of the corporation’s title alone.
